callback_protocol: source-composed caller contract; arbitrary valid callback programs remain their own semantics, not a finite builtin dtype table

families.name: Public dispatch and native argument ordering
remaining_obligations: CPython allocation/refcount failure and outer protocol implementations remain integration obligations; no query failure class is globally suppressed.
rules: Outer NumPy array-function dispatch precedes native default: result_type relevant operands=all; can_cast relevant operand=from_ only; promote_types has native two-positional-only descriptor arguments. Preserve override call/return/NotImplemented and exception lifecycle separately from native predicate suppression.

Outer lookup phase: exact-basic-type skips and exact-ndarray cached method path; otherwise type-object special lookup (instance-only method ignored). ANY lookup exception is cleared and treated absent by get_array_function. Present None/noncallable is an override and fails at invocation; successful return unchanged, NotImplemented defers, exhausting implementations raisesTypeError. Invocation errors propagate; this is separate from predicate resolver-error-toFalse projection.

Native keyword parser initializes/caches argument names, rejects excessive positional args, resolves ALL keyword names/duplicates in user keyword order before any converter. Unknown keyword/duplicate errors therefore precede even invalid dtype converters.

After mapping succeeds, converters run in declaration parameter order, irrespective of supplied keyword order. Only after conversions complete does parser detect missing required args. An invalid optional casting parameter can precede a missing required-argument error.

can_cast converter order: from_ stored raw, to via DescrConverter2, casting via CastingConverter; targetNULL check occurs after parser, before source classification. Source ndarray uses C descriptor; NumPy scalar reads dtype attribute and requires actual descriptor; Python numeric value rejected; other source uses DescrConverter2.
promote_types converts positional descriptors in order through Converter2, then rejects eitherNULL; only then calls PromoteTypes and decrefs descriptors on success/failure.

result_type rejects zero args ValueError before workspace allocation. It classifies original args left-to-right: retain ndarray; NumPy/Python scalar ->PyArray_FROM_O plus exact Python-scalar temporary marker; other object ->DescrConverter. Only after all conversion succeeds call ResultType, then release temporaries.

families.name: Complete casting-mode conversion boundary
rules: Only Unicode strings and bytes are accepted. Bytes are decoded using CPython default encoding/error policy; failed decoding is replaced with ValueError by string_converter_helper. Other object types ->TypeError. Unicode UTF8 encoding failures propagate.

Exact case-sensitive spellings no/equiv/safe/same_kind/unsafe are accepted for can_cast; prefix/suffix/whitespace/NUL-extended strings are invalid ValueError. same_value is accepted only by the separate SameValue converter used by ndarray.astype, not by can_cast.

Parser failure without pending exception produces ValueError; a parser/UTF8 exception already present is retained. Enum values are source-defined; SAME_VALUE is flag64|UNSAFE, not another ordered sixth level.

MinCastSafety: negative input ->-1; strip same-value bit, choose larger/less-safe base enum, retain same-value bit only if BOTH inputs had it. No/equiv/safe/same_kind/unsafe form enum0..4 with lower=safer.

families.name: Descriptor versus DType-class conversion
remaining_obligations: Exact CPython/ctypes ABI sizes and platform C-int/intp constants remain reference-build parameters.
Recursive structured constructors and arbitrary ctypes graphs are source-captured/compositional; full accepted-input/error matrix remains unmaterialized.
rules: DescrConverter(None) ->default dtype descriptor; Converter2(None) ->success withNULL (public promote_types/can_cast then reject). A descriptor object is retained by reference; type objects, bytes/Unicode strings, tuple/list/dict forms take distinct ordered branches; ndarray object is rejected as dtype spec.

Type conversion recognizes NumPy scalar subclasses then exact Python int->NPY_INTP, float->DOUBLE, complex->CDOUBLE, bool->BOOL, bytes->STRING, str->UNICODE, memoryview->VOID, object->OBJECT. Other types first try registered scalar mapping/default descriptor, then dtype hook, ctypes, finally object. This is not the weak scalar VALUE promotion path.

Hook precedence is instance optional __numpy_dtype__, falling back to dtype ONLY when absent. Lookup exceptions propagate. Present None/invalid value ->ValueError, not absent. A type object whose attribute value itself exposes __get__ can defer via NotImplemented; valid descriptor returns unchanged. ctypes fallback runs after hooks and validates returned descriptor type.

String parsing checks comma/repetition syntax first, then byteorder prefix (| becomes=), datetime format, one-character typecode or kind+nonnegative length. Unicode length multiplies by4 with C-int limit; byte/void sizes differ. Fallback registered typeDict lookup is separate, removed aliases int0/uint0/void0/object0/str0/bytes0/bool8 get specific TypeError. Native-equivalent byteorder canonicalizes to=; byteorder-irrelevant | is retained where dtype uses it.

Tuple requires length2: resolve base first, then inherit-tuple attempt; unsized base interprets itemsize, metadata dictionary may merge, empty-tuple subshape decays to base, otherwise subarray. Subarray rejects finalize-bearing base (for example StringDType), negative/non-C-int dimensions, count/byte-size overflow; stores owned base and immutable integer shape tuple.

Structured list/dict conversion has named recursive branches with object-field overlap/alignment/title/offset/itemsize checks captured in exact function witnesses. Dict missing-key paths can clear lookup errors and fall back to field-dict parsing; do not apply an all-hook-errors-propagate rule to those phases.

ctypes probe npy_ctypes_check imports/calls the Python checker, truth-tests it, and clears ANY failure at this probe boundary to false/not-ctypes. After a positive probe, dtype_from_ctypes_type failures propagate. Its exact body maps arrays to subarray descriptors; rejects pointer types; structures reject bitfields, use explicit pack offsets or aligned fields; unions use offset0 and actual ctypes.sizeof; scalar types use explicit endian attributes. Platform ctypes.sizeof/alignment remain parameters. Struct versus union bitfield handling has distinct source unpack/error behavior.

DTypeOrDescrRequired allows DType classes except the abstract np.dtype class; ordinary descriptor conversion then extraction can treat legacy flexible S0/U0/unbound temporal prototypes as a class plus no fixed instance. Optional(None) leaves caller-initialized output unchanged. S versus S0 distinction is explicitly not reliably preserved by these compatibility paths.

families.name: Common dtype class and multi-input callback order
remaining_obligations: User-defined nontransitive or order-sensitive callbacks require their actual program semantics; no guarantee beyond source algorithm.
rules: CommonDType identical classes return same class without callbacks. Otherwise call left.common_dtype(right); only NotImplemented calls right.common_dtype(left). NULL/error propagates; both NotImplemented ->DTypePromotionError. No automatic object fallback in this API.

PromoteDTypeSequence is the source pairwise most-knowledgeable reduction, not left-fold of promote_types or a universal LUB. It can swap high/low candidates on NotImplemented, discard candidates whose result is the low class, then call chosen main class on remaining candidates and combine results. User callback order/transitivity requirements are observable.

Legacy builtin default callback handles weak PyComplex/PyFloat/PyLong explicitly; otherwise defers to higher legacy typenum and consults source-initialized promotion table. Object common_dtype returns object for every peer. Fixed string/Unicode only accept legacy numeric (and Unicode accepts String) as specified. Datetime+timedelta can choose datetime class, but later casts may reject; class promotion is not operational compatibility.

Custom common_dtype callback bodies are user-supplied behavior under the registration protocol; the caller composition/invocation/NotImplemented/error order is the contract. No hardcoded enumeration can replace arbitrary valid custom callbacks.

families.name: Two-descriptor promotion and metadata preservation
remaining_obligations: Byte layout results need actual ABI alignment/itemsize parameters; safe query is not an ownership/view mutation authorization.
rules: Fast path retains IDENTICAL descriptor object only for legacy native-byteorder nonVOID. It preserves metadata/identity. Otherwise resolve common class. Nonparametric common class returns its default descriptor (metadata lost), not first operand descriptor.

Parametric common class casts left descriptor to class then right; missing casts/resolve errors are wrapped/chained by CastDescrToDType TypeError. Then call common_instance(left,right), release intermediate descriptors and common class. Same-class CastDescrToDType retains descriptor; nonparametric/nonabstract target can use default descriptor without resolving cast.

S/U common_instance chooses larger elsize, left on tie, then ensure canonical native byteorder. Void unstructured equal length retains first; differing length ->DTypePromotionError. Both structured call _internal._promote_fields; both subarrays require equal shape and recursively promote base; mixed structured/subarray/plain invalid combinations fail.

Structured fields require same ordered names and matching titles; recursively promote field descriptors, align if EITHER input aligned. Padding/offsets recomputed. Identity/metadata retained only if identical inputs, promoted fields retain identity, resulting itemsize and offsets unchanged. Canonical void recursively normalizes bases/fields and strips unnecessary padding while preserving aligned-versus-unaligned policy.

families.name: Exact Python weak scalars and result_type workflow
rules: Single total operand bypasses promotion and calls ensure_canonical on its discovered array/descriptor dtype. Python-int range can affect this descriptor: try signed longlong; choose intp when it fits, else longlong; try unsigned longlong; beyond it use object. Errors at these discovery conversion attempts are cleared per source.

For multiple inputs, descriptors are placed FIRST in internal arrays, then array operands, preserving each sublist order rather than original interleaving. Exact Python int/float/complex temporary flags choose abstract PyLong/PyFloat/PyComplex classes with no descriptor; ordinary arrays/scalars retain concrete descriptors. bool and subclasses are not these exact Python weak tags.

Abstract common class is replaced with default descriptor class; parametric common result converts and combines only retained concrete descriptors, skipping weak descriptorless values. If nonparametric or no concrete result, use default descriptor. Always preserve source cleanup/error ordering.

Therefore arbitrary Python-int value can affect SINGLE-input result_type but generally does not provide precision/value-based min_scalar_type promotion in MULTI-input weak path. Descriptor TYPE objects such as int are strong default dtype specs, separate from scalar values. This policy query does not prove later scalar conversion fits eventual dtype.

Weak class fallback for legacy user types can try uint8/int8/default-int (float:half then double; complex:cfloat then cdouble), with source-specific error clearing/retry behavior. Caller phase/callback order is explicit, not a blanket error suppression policy.

families.name: Predicate cast resolution, descriptor parameters and error disposition
rules: GetCastingImpl first uses within-class cache or registered source->target dictionary; missing entry lazily creates generic object/void or legacy wrapper cast under a critical section, stores result (including None). Nonlegacy unknown casts return None; missing builtin cast is RuntimeError. Source-state and callback effects are observable; this is not a pure numeric payload kernel.

CheckCastSafety returns True immediately when advertised method casting is already within requested relation; resolver is NOT called. Otherwise resolve_descriptors supplies loop descriptors and view_offset; changed descriptor identities trigger secondary GetCastInfo checks in source order, combining safety and invalidating view offset when offsets differ.

CanCastTypeTo and ordinary CanCastArrayTo convert unsized S0/U0 target (without subarray) to target-class/no-fixed-descriptor. Any negative result/error from CheckCastSafety is cleared and returns False, irrespective of exception type or origin. This boundary includes errors from resolver callbacks. Dtype conversion/parser or OUTER array-function invocation errors occur earlier and propagate instead.

Internal arrays with exact Python-literal temporary flags take a separate weak-literal casting branch; arbitrary user-visible0D NumPy scalars/arrays do not receive value-based min_scalar_type treatment. Public can_cast rejects Python numeric value operands before this predicate. Do not infer a normal user can create those internal flags via ndarray input.

can_cast True only reports policy acceptance; advertised-safe path can bypass output-descriptor discovery and later conversion may still fail. Safe includes documented rounding-loss integer-to-float cases; it is not a proof of exact payload representability. same_value remains a separate actual-cast check.

families.name: All source legacy table cells and numeric casting registration
remaining_obligations: C sizes, endian/alignment, longdouble representation and available compiled kernels require exact build receipts.
Illustrative ABI matrices are analytical models only, not the host or a released NumPy environment.
rules: can_cast_table.h has exactly24x24 cells. Machine extraction expands every initializer/macro to a boolean expression over NPY_SIZEOF_* compile-time ABI values; no host ABI value is observed here. IFITS intentionally accepts equal-size integer->float when source size>=double size; this is a compatibility policy, not exact value preservation.

initialize_casting_tables builds scalar-kind/next-larger/smallest-kind mappings then class promotion table: numeric safe-direction preference, otherwise successive larger same-kind then larger kind; special string/Unicode/void/datetime/timedelta table entries defer except object. Public callbacks override these class entries and descriptors carry further parameters.

Numeric cast registration covers bool and legacy numeric pairs. Equal kind and elsize chooses copy/byteswap descriptor resolver; table-safe chooses SAFE, otherwise kind-order relation chooses SAME_KIND or UNSAFE. All registered numeric modes carry SAME_VALUE_FLAG as potential runtime-validation capability, not proof every payload cast is same_value.

Simple numeric resolver ensures canonical loop descriptors; same numerical type with byteorder difference requires EQUIV, matching byteorder can be NO with view_offset0. Descriptor view safety does not authorize arbitrary memory mutation. Complex->noncomplex nonbool actual loop can warn; query itself need not execute that loop.

families.name: Structured, string, object and temporal cast boundaries
rules: Fixed string casts resolve width from source dtype: bool5, integers decimal bound by width/sign, standard floats32, longdouble48, complex doubled, fixed S/V bytes, U bytes/4; target U scales4 with C-int limit. Explicit too-short output reduces SAFE to SAME_KIND. Arbitrary object values require distinct discovery/coercion, not fixed type-only width proof.

Structured->structured cast compares equal field counts and fields by ORDER, then names/titles mismatch limits safety to SAFE; recursively combines per-field casts. Different offsets/elsize can make EQUIV; a single shared nonnegative view offset must fit within original itemsize. Field count mismatch or helper failure yields invalid/negative result; public can_cast turns itFalse at its boundary.

Void same size NO/view0; widening SAFE; narrowing SAME_KIND/view0. Subarray shapes and base-itemsize relation control candidate view; base cast safety combines with outer-layout safety. Structured/nonstructured paths have explicit resolvers and are not generic object casts.

Generic any->object is SAFE; object->other is UNSAFE. Parametric object targets without specified instance can fail; StringDType has its own exception/default handling. Query True does not inspect all object payloads or ensure each object converts later.

Legacy can_cast_*_units/metadata helpers are NOT the final registered query resolver. Actual within-dtype casts are registered with time_to_time_resolve_descriptors: identical descriptor ->NO/view0; equal metadata OR the exact source metric-prefix integer-quotient predicates ->NO when byteorder matches, EQUIV otherwise; generic source ->SAFE, generic destination ->UNSAFE; timedelta nonlinear/linear barrier ->UNSAFE; remaining forward unit ordering with divisibility ->SAFE, otherwise SAME_KIND. Cross datetime/timedelta resolver returnsUNSAFE. Requested UNSAFE can bypass these resolver checks through advertised-safety fastpath.

The metric-prefix predicate uses integer division, not an exact-ratio test: same-byteorder2001ms to2s satisfies quotient1000 and selectsNO by source despite unequal mathematical durations. This is an explicit source/documented-no-cast question requiring frozen binary comparison, not an approved exclusion or reference-bug waiver. Temporal promotion GCD is a separate common_instance policy, strict for timedelta input and relaxed for datetime, with TypeError nonlinear incompatibility and OverflowError multiplier/conversion-factor overflow paths.

Unsigned arithmetic and explicit overflow masks in datetime helpers are part of source semantics; do not replace them with an unbounded-integer claim for all valid descriptors. ABI/config errors and malformed internal metadata require their upstream construction contract.

families.name: StringDType and public custom dtype callback protocols
remaining_obligations: All custom callback registration legality, allocator/NA equality side effects and clear/finalize integration require source-to-implementation/runtime coverage; no implementation ABI approval inferred.
rules: StringDType common_dtype accepts fixed Unicode peer; other distinct peers defer NotImplemented, while identical class is handled by generic identity fast path. common_instance negotiates NA/coerce parameters and creates a new descriptor; incompatible NA/coercion can raise TypeError.

StringDType finalization/allocator lifetime is descriptor-state-sensitive; subarray dtype rejects finalize-bearing base because no attached array could finalize it. Managed string versus fixed-width S/U is an admitted distinct family, not an unsupported dtype dropped from scope.

StringDType->fixed-width unspecified target size raises TypeError in resolver; public predicate can suppress resolver error toFalse when resolution runs, or return an advertised-safe answer without invoking resolver if fast path applies. Preserve exact mode/callback phase.

Custom DType callback invocation, returned descriptors, temporary refs, data finalization and clear/fill loops require equivalent first-party interfaces. Caller semantics are compositional over user callback programs; no foreign NumPy runtime may stand in for them. C API/ABI exposure is an explicit planned interop obligation, not an approved binary-ABI compatibility claim.
